subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is a Port?
a: A 4-byte address that identifies a computer
b: An unsigned 2-byte integer that lets the OS distinguish network-communicating processes
c: The domain name (hostname) of the server
explanation: A port is an unsigned 2-byte integer that helps the OS distinguish network-communicating processes.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What are the lengths of the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, respectively?
explanation: IPv4 = 4 bytes (e.g. 192.143.5.1), IPv6 = 16 bytes.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is a characteristic of TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)?
b: Sends independent datagrams with no delivery guarantee
c: No connection needs to be established before sending
d: Connection-based; guarantees a reliable data stream thanks to the acknowledgment mechanism
explanation: TCP is connection-based and reliable thanks to acknowledgments.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which statement about UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is correct?
a: Sends independent datagrams with no guarantee of delivery or correct ordering
explanation: UDP sends independent datagrams with no delivery/ordering guarantee; the app must handle lost, duplicated and out-of-order packets itself.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is a URI (Uniform Resource Identifier)?
a: Just the IP address of the server
b: The physical path of a file on disk
c: A specially formatted string describing a resource on the internet or LAN (URL and URN are subsets of URI)
explanation: A URI is a string describing a resource; URL and URN are subsets of it.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is a characteristic of URN (e.g. `urn:isbn:0451450523`)?
a: It tells the network location where the resource resides
b: It is a URI using the "urn" scheme; it identifies independently of location and does not imply the resource is available for access
d: It guarantees the resource is always accessible
explanation: URN uses the "urn" scheme, is location-independent and does not imply the resource is available. URL is the one that indicates location.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which class is the abstract base class of the request/response model (HTTP, FTP, `file:`) in a protocol-agnostic way?
explanation: WebRequest is the abstract base class for HTTP, FTP and `file:`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: How does a client obtain a `WebResponse` object?
explanation: The client does not create a WebResponse itself; it gets one via `GetResponse()`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: How does HttpClient differ from WebRequest/WebClient?
a: It is only used for the FTP protocol
b: It is designed for web APIs/REST, allows plugging in custom message handlers (mockable during unit tests), and each instance has its own connection pool
c: It does not support asynchronous programming
d: It is required to be based on WebRequest in every version of .NET
explanation: HttpClient fits web APIs/REST, has custom message handlers (mockable during unit tests), and each instance has its own connection pool.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which method sends a GET and asynchronously returns the response body as a `string`?
explanation: `GetStringAsync` sends a GET and returns the body as a string.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What task does the Domain Name System (DNS) perform?
a: Translates human-readable internet addresses (domain names) into the corresponding IP addresses
explanation: DNS maps domain names to IP addresses.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What are the three components of DNS?
d: Name Space, Globally Distributed Database (Name Servers), Resolver
explanation: Name Space, Globally Distributed Database (Name Servers), Resolver.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which class does the server side use to listen for and accept incoming TCP connections?
explanation: TcpListener listens for and accepts connections; TcpClient is the side that connects.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which method of `TcpClient` returns a `NetworkStream` for sending/receiving data?
explanation: `GetStream()` returns the `NetworkStream` used to send/receive data.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which method of the `Socket` class puts a socket into the listening state?
explanation: `Listen()` puts the Socket into the listening state; `Accept()` creates a new Socket for an incoming connection.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: A mono-processor von Neumann system (input-processing-output) is also known as which model in Flynn's Taxonomy?
explanation: SISD (single instruction, single data); it hits the von Neumann bottleneck.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does symmetrical multiprocessing (SMP) mean?
a: A master processor acts as a manager distributing tasks to the other processors
b: Any free processor/core can execute a task
c: Only one core can be used
d: Only software optimized for multiprocessing can run
explanation: SMP: any free processor/core can run the task. Option A describes AMP (asymmetrical multiprocessing).

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the maximum number of tasks a quad-core processor with Hyper-Threading (HT) can run at the same time?
explanation: Quad-core x HT (2 logical cores per core) = 8 tasks at once.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which company developed Hyper-Threading (launched on Xeon in 2002)?
explanation: Intel developed HT, launching it on Xeon in 2002.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which architecture enables true parallelism and is used by most systems today?
explanation: MIMD provides true parallelism and is used by most modern systems.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which architecture is commonly used for fault tolerance, e.g. the computer controlling a space shuttle?
explanation: MISD is used for fault tolerance, e.g. the computer controlling a space shuttle.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the characteristic of Serial Computing?
a: Instructions run one after another on a single processor; only one instruction is executed at a time
b: The problem is split into parts that run concurrently
c: Multiple processors are used at once
d: A central coordination mechanism is required
explanation: Serial: instructions run sequentially on a single processor.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the limitation of Parallel Computing?
a: It always costs more than serial
b: It cannot be used for real-time simulation
c: It can only run on one CPU
d: Communication and synchronization between sub-tasks is difficult to implement
explanation: Communication and synchronization between sub-tasks is hard.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which namespaces contain the TPL (Task Parallel Library)?
explanation: TPL lives in `System.Threading` and `System.Threading.Tasks`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which class do you use when you want a task to return a value?
explanation: `Task` returns no result; you need `Task<TResult>`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does `Task.WhenAll(Task[])` do?
a: Creates a task that completes when all the tasks in the array have completed
b: Completes as soon as the first task finishes
d: Runs the tasks one by one sequentially
explanation: `WhenAll` completes when all the child tasks are done.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which method do you use to turn a LINQ query into PLINQ?
explanation: `AsParallel()` is the entry point of PLINQ.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the PLINQ `AsOrdered` operator do?
a: Ignores the order of the source data
b: Asks PLINQ to preserve the order of the source sequence
c: Limits the maximum number of processors
d: Forces the query to run sequentially
explanation: `AsOrdered` preserves the source sequence order; `AsUnordered` does not need to.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which is a correct note when using PLINQ?
a: PLINQ is always faster than LINQ
b: You should write to a file/database directly inside a PLINQ query
c: Parallelism has overhead so performance must be measured; `AsParallel()` does not guarantee that the query definitely runs in parallel
d: PLINQ always runs in parallel when `AsParallel()` is present
explanation: Parallelism has overhead and must be measured; avoid non-thread-safe I/O; `AsParallel` does not guarantee parallel execution.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What do `async` and `await` give you?
a: Writing an async method is almost as easy as a synchronous one, and the calling thread is not blocked waiting
b: They force you to create a new thread for every statement
explanation: `async/await` lets you write asynchronous code that looks nearly synchronous; the calling thread is not blocked.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Who developed the SOLID principles?
c: Robert C. Martin (essay in 2000); the SOLID acronym was coined by Michael Feathers
explanation: Robert C. Martin (2000); Michael Feathers coined the SOLID acronym.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the S (Single Responsibility Principle) say?
a: A class should have only one responsibility (one reason to change)
b: Open for extension, closed for modification
c: A subtype can replace its base type
d: Many specialized interfaces are better than one general interface
explanation: S: one class, one responsibility.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the O (Open/Closed Principle) say?
a: A class has only one responsibility
b: A subtype can replace its base type
d: A software entity is open for extension and closed for modification
explanation: O: open for extension, closed for modification.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the L (Liskov Substitution Principle) say?
a: Many small interfaces are better than one large interface
b: An object can be replaced by an instance of a subtype without making the program incorrect
c: A class has only one responsibility
explanation: L: a subtype can substitute without breaking the program.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the I (Interface Segregation Principle) say?
a: Use one very large general interface for every client
c: Many specialized interfaces for each client are better than one general-purpose interface
d: High-level modules depend on low-level modules
explanation: I: many specialized interfaces beat one general interface.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the D (Dependency Inversion Principle) say?
a: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions
b: Low-level modules must depend on high-level modules
d: Do not use interfaces in the design
explanation: D: both high-level and low-level depend on abstractions.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Class `Notification` directly creates `new Email()` in its constructor. What is this?
d: Tightly coupled: to send another kind of notification you have to modify `Notification`
explanation: `new Email()` in the constructor is tightly coupled, violating DIP and OCP.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the relationship between DIP and IoC (Inversion of Control)?
b: DIP is a principle (theory); IoC is a pattern with concrete steps to make code DIP-friendly
d: DIP is a pattern, IoC is a principle
explanation: DIP is a principle/theory; IoC is a pattern with concrete steps to make code DIP-friendly.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is Dependency Injection (DI)?
a: Creating an object with `new` inside the class that uses it
b: Using a static class for every dependency
c: A way of implementing IoC by injecting a concrete implementation into the class that is using an abstraction (interface)
explanation: DI is a way to implement IoC: inject an implementation into the class that uses an interface.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What are the three basic capabilities of a DI Container?
explanation: Registration, Resolution (create and inject), Disposition (lifetime management).

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which service lifetime creates a new instance every time it is requested?
explanation: Transient creates a new instance per request; Singleton uses a single instance; Scoped is limited to one context.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: How does Ambient Context provide a dependency?
b: Through a static accessor, avoiding cluttering the API with cross-cutting concerns
c: Passing it as a method parameter
explanation: Ambient Context provides the dependency through a static accessor.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which DI pattern ensures the dependency is always available because every caller is required to provide it through the constructor?
explanation: Constructor Injection: the most common one; it ensures the dependency exists when the object is created.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the drawback of Property Injection?
a: It hides the dependency and the property can be null, so null checks are needed everywhere it is used
b: It ensures the dependency is always present at construction
c: It forces you to change the constructor
d: It can only be used with static classes
explanation: Property Injection hides the dependency and it can be null, easily causing a `NullReferenceException`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: When the dependency changes on every call (a different dependency per operation), which pattern should you use?
a: A dependency fixed for the whole lifetime of the object
d: Method Injection (pass the dependency as a method parameter)
explanation: Method Injection: the dependency differs per call and is passed as a parameter.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is a characteristic of ASP.NET Core?
a: It only runs on Windows and requires `System.Web.dll`
b: Free, open-source, cross-platform, lightweight modular architecture and no dependency on `System.Web.dll`
d: It can only run on IIS
explanation: Free, open-source, cross-platform, modular, and no longer dependent on `System.Web.dll`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What are the limitations of ASP.NET Web Forms that led to needing a new framework?
a: Easy to test and complete control over HTML
d: Lack of testability, a complex stateful model and little control over the generated HTML
explanation: Web Forms: lack of testability, complex stateful model, little control over HTML.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What are the two main tasks of Routing?
a: Map an incoming request to a Controller Action; generate the corresponding outgoing URLs for the action
b: Render the view and save to the database
c: Encrypt the URL and compress the response
explanation: Routing maps request to action and generates outgoing URLs.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: In the pattern `{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}`, what does the `?` in `id?` mean?
explanation: `?` means the parameter is optional.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the role of the Controller in MVC?
a: It only renders the HTML interface
b: Handles user interactions/requests, runs the necessary logic and returns a response (orchestrating the logic flow)
c: It only stores data into the database
d: It only contains CSS and JavaScript
explanation: The Controller orchestrates the logic flow and returns the response.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the responsibility of the View in MVC?
d: Only rendering the model to the user; it should not contain processing logic
explanation: The View only renders; it does not process logic.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is a ViewModel?
a: A class containing only the properties the view needs; it is optional and helps expose only the necessary data
b: A class that must be present in every view
explanation: A ViewModel holds the data specific to the view; it is optional.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the condition for an Action method?
c: It must be public and must not be static
explanation: An action method must be `public` and must not be `static`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: If a view is not found in the `Views/<ControllerName>` folder, where does the framework look next?
explanation: A view not found in `Views/<Controller>` is searched for next in `Views/Shared`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is Model Binding?
c: Creating a table in the database
d: Mapping data from the HTTP request (form, route, query string, body) into the parameters of an action method
explanation: Model binding maps request data into the action parameters.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: When does Model Validation take place?
a: After model binding and before the action executes; errors are stored in `ModelState`
b: After the action has already finished running
d: It only takes place on the client
explanation: Validation runs after binding and before the action; the result lives in `ModelState`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the `[Compare]` attribute used for?
b: Checking a value within a range
c: Checking that two properties in the model match (e.g. Password and ConfirmPassword)
explanation: `[Compare]` matches two properties against each other.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Compare ViewData and ViewBag?
a: ViewBag is a key/value dictionary, ViewData is dynamic
b: ViewData is a key/value dictionary; ViewBag is similar but accessed through dynamic properties
d: Only ViewBag can pass data from the controller to the view
explanation: ViewData is a dictionary; ViewBag is a wrapper accessed using dynamic properties.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is TempData used for?
a: It only exists within a single view
c: It only exists on the client side
d: Temporary storage, usually for one-time messages/passing data between actions; `TempData.Keep()` keeps the data after the view is rendered
explanation: TempData holds temporary/one-time data; `Keep()` retains it after rendering.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the storage scope of `HttpContext.Items`?
a: Only within a single request; it is discarded after the request has been processed
b: Across many requests of the same user
explanation: `HttpContext.Items` lives only for a single request.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is Razor Pages?
a: A framework that runs entirely client-side
b: A framework that can only be used on Windows
c: A server-side, page-focused framework for building dynamic websites, based on MVC and available since .NET Core 2.0
d: A library that replaces the C# language
explanation: Server-side, page-focused, available since .NET Core 2.0.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which two files make up a Razor Page together with its PageModel?
explanation: `.cshtml` + `.cshtml.cs`, mapped 1-1.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the naming convention for handler methods in Razor Pages?
d: The "On" prefix: `OnGet()`, `OnPost()`; `OnGet` and `OnGetAsync` are considered the same handler
explanation: The "On" + verb convention: `OnGet`, `OnPost`; the async version is the same handler.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is `_Layout.cshtml` used for?
b: Serving as the template for the content pages that reference it (the consistent UI of the site)
c: Running code after every content page
explanation: `_Layout` is the shared template for the pages.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the role of `_ViewStart.cshtml`?
b: Participating in routing like a normal page
c: Holding code that runs after the code of the content page in the same folder/subfolder; a convenient place to specify the layout
explanation: `_ViewStart` runs after the content page code, making it convenient for specifying the layout.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is `_ViewImports.cshtml` used for?
a: Gathering the shared directives (`@using`, `@addTagHelper`, `@inject`, `@model`...) for the Razor pages
explanation: `_ViewImports` gathers the shared directives.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is a characteristic of Partial Pages?
d: They do not participate in routing; rendered with `<partial name="_MenuPartial" />`
explanation: A partial page does not participate in routing; it is rendered with `<partial />`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the PageModel in Razor Pages?
a: An implementation of the MVVM pattern
b: An implementation of the Page Controller pattern (one page to one controller), acting as both controller and view model
c: An implementation of a Front Controller handling every request of the site
explanation: PageModel = the Page Controller pattern; not MVVM, not a Front Controller.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: When should you use a View Component instead of a partial page or a tag helper?
a: When you only need static HTML
b: When you do not need unit tests
c: When you need logic to fetch data (file, database, web service); the class inherits `ViewComponent` and has an `Invoke` method
d: When you want to replace routing
explanation: A View Component is used when you need logic to fetch data; the class inherits `ViewComponent` and has `Invoke`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: In Razor Pages routing, at which URL(s) can the `Index.cshtml` file in the root `Pages` folder be accessed?
explanation: `Index.cshtml` is accessible via both `/` and `/Index`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Why is server-side validation still needed when client-side validation already exists?
b: Server-side is faster so it replaces the client
d: Client-side is very easy to bypass; the server runs the validation attributes and `ModelState.IsValid` returns `false` if there are errors
explanation: Client-side validation is easy to bypass, so the server must check again. Tester tip: try disabling JavaScript and then submitting invalid data.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the `[BindProperty]` attribute on a public property of a PageModel do?
a: Attaches the property to a handler method
b: Binds the posted form value into the property (convenient for using values outside the handler and for binding with tag helpers)
d: Defines the route for the page
explanation: `[BindProperty]` binds the form value into the PageModel property.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What are Tag Helpers in Razor Pages?
a: A JavaScript library for manipulating the DOM
b: A tool for generating database code
c: Reusable components that automatically generate HTML for specific tags; enabled with `@addTagHelper *, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.TagHelpers`
explanation: A Tag Helper automatically generates HTML for specific tags and is enabled with `@addTagHelper`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which statement about Session state in Razor Pages is correct?
a: It is not enabled by default; it must be enabled in the Startup/app configuration file, and a cookie is used to tie the requests together into one session
d: It is only stored on the client side
explanation: Session is not enabled by default and uses a cookie to link the requests together.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What happens to a request that does not go through HTTPS when the `RequireHttps` attribute is used?
c: It is always redirected to HTTPS regardless of which verb is used
d: A GET request is redirected to the HTTPS version; other verbs (e.g. POST) receive 403 Forbidden
explanation: GET is redirected to HTTPS; other verbs such as POST get 403 Forbidden.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which two words is the name "Blazor" built from?
explanation: Blazor = Browser + Razor.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: In Blazor Server, through what are the UI interactions handled?
explanation: Blazor Server handles UI through a SignalR connection.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which kind of application is Blazor WebAssembly best suited for?
a: An internal application that needs a constant connection to the server
b: An application that only runs on the server
c: An offline-capable or public application (the first download is large, but afterwards no server interaction is needed)
d: An application that does not use C#
explanation: WASM suits offline-capable or public apps; the first-time download is heavy.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: In which file is a Blazor component usually defined, and how is it used?
d: A `.razor` file, used like an element: `<MyComponent />`
explanation: The component lives in a `.razor` file and is used like `<MyComponent />`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which directive declares the route `/todo` for a component?
explanation: `@page "/todo"` declares the route.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What kind of binding does `<input @bind="newTodo" />` perform?
a: Two-way binding between the input box and the `newTodo` variable
explanation: `@bind` is two-way binding.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which attribute attaches a C# method to the click event of a button?
explanation: `@onclick` attaches a C# method to the click event.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the role of the `Routes.razor` file in a Blazor Web App project?
c: It is the entry point that starts the server
d: It configures the Blazor router (`App.razor` is the root component)
explanation: `Routes.razor` configures the router; `App.razor` is the root component.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the `_Imports.razor` file used for?
b: Declaring the namespaces commonly shared by the components
d: Being the entry point of the application
explanation: `_Imports.razor` declares the shared namespaces.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What are Cascading Values (cascading parameters) used for in Blazor?
explanation: Cascading parameters share data between nested components.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the line `@rendermode InteractiveServer` at the top of a component do?
b: Forces the component to run on WebAssembly
c: Turns on interactivity for the component in Interactive Server mode
explanation: `@rendermode InteractiveServer` turns on Server-style interactivity.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which command applies the migrations to the database in the Movie demo (EF Core)?
a: `dotnet ef migrations add "InitialDB"` (this command only creates the migration file)
explanation: `database update` applies the migrations; `migrations add` only creates the migration file.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the `[Column(TypeName = "decimal(18, 2)")]` attribute on the `Price` property do?
a: Formats the display on the UI
b: Specifies the column type in the database
c: Forces the user to enter a price
explanation: `[Column(TypeName=...)]` specifies the column type in the DB.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: How does "Pushing" differ from "Pulling"?
a: Push means being notified of what is new, instead of having to go ask what is new (Pull)
b: Push means the client constantly asks the server
c: Pull means the server sends data down to the client by itself
d: The two concepts are the same
explanation: Push = being told what is new; Pull = going to ask.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What is the transport fallback order in SignalR?
explanation: WebSockets to Server-Sent Events to Long Polling.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: How do you create a Hub in SignalR?
d: Declare a class that inherits from `Hub` and add public methods
explanation: A Hub is a class inheriting from `Hub`; its public methods are what clients can call.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What do you need in order to configure SignalR in `Program.cs`?
b: `AddSignalR()` registers the services; `MapHub<ChatHub>("/chatHub")` maps the hub to a URL endpoint
c: Only installing the JavaScript library on the client
explanation: `AddSignalR()` + `MapHub<T>(url)`.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: On which objects does `Clients.Others` invoke the method?
a: All connected clients except the client that called the hub method
b: Only the client that called the hub method
explanation: `Others` = every client except the caller.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does `Context.ConnectionId` return?
c: A unique ID assigned by SignalR to each connection
explanation: `ConnectionId` is the unique ID of each connection.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: How do you fix the "magic string" drawback of `SendAsync("ReceiveMessage", ...)`?
d: A strongly typed hub with `Hub<T>` to avoid runtime errors caused by a wrong method name
explanation: `Hub<T>` catches a wrong name at compile time instead of causing a runtime error.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: What does the `[HubMethodName("SendMessageToUser")]` attribute do?
b: Specifies the name the client uses to call the method, instead of the default .NET method name
c: Hides the method from the client
explanation: `[HubMethodName]` renames the method that the client calls.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: In `OnDisconnectedAsync(Exception exception)`, when is the `exception` parameter `null`?
a: When the client disconnects intentionally (e.g. calls `connection.stop()`)
b: When there is a network failure
explanation: `null` on an intentional disconnect; there is an exception when the disconnect is caused by an error such as a network fault.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: Which statement about Hub filters is correct?
a: They only existed before ASP.NET Core 3.1
b: They only run on the client side
c: They exist since ASP.NET Core 5.0, implement `IHubFilter` with `InvokeMethodAsync`; global filters run before local filters
explanation: Hub filters exist since ASP.NET Core 5.0, implement `IHubFilter`; global runs before local.

subject: PRN222-EN
content: How does MessagePack compare to JSON in SignalR?
a: It is larger and slower than JSON
b: It is easier to read with the naked eye
d: It is a compact binary serialization and is faster (e.g. in the slide: JSON 27 bytes, MessagePack 18 bytes)
explanation: MessagePack is smaller and faster than JSON (18 bytes versus 27 bytes in the example).

subject: PRN222-EN
content: In the Entity Framework + SignalR lab, why do we call `Clients.All.SendAsync("LoadProducts")` after `SaveChangesAsync()`?
a: To save the data into the database
b: To tell every client to reload the product list (the client calls `LoadProdData()` and redraws the table), keeping the data synchronized in real time
explanation: It tells every client to reload the list so the data stays synchronized in real time.
